themes_detail.label: Street noise surge
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints spiked to 86 THIS WEEK, a 399% increase versus the 8-week baseline average of 17.2 weekly complaints (z-score: 5.12), suggesting a new and acute noise-generation event or pattern in the district.
evidence: 86 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 17.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (399% spike)
z-score of 5.12 indicates statistically significant anomaly
No equivalent spike in residential noise (1,770 total over 90 days), suggesting outdoor source
reporting_angles: Ground-truth reporting: what construction, street work, or outdoor activity is generating complaints this specific week?
Interview affected residents on streets with highest complaint density to identify common source

themes_detail.label: Park rule violations spike
themes_detail.summary: Park rule violation complaints jumped to 3 THIS WEEK, a 2,300% increase from the 0.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 8.69), signaling a possible new pattern of unauthorized park activity or enforcement action.
evidence: 3 park rule violation complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2,300% spike)
Coincides with spike in animal-in-park complaints (3 complaints 2 weeks ago, 1,100% increase), suggesting related park activity
z-score of 8.69 indicates extreme statistical rarity
reporting_angles: Contact Parks Department to identify which park(s) are seeing violations and what enforcement actions are underway
Investigate whether off-leash dogs, encampments, or other specific violations are driving complaints

themes_detail.label: Graffiti explosion
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints peaked at 16 three weeks ago, a 1,064% increase from the 1.4 weekly baseline (z-score: 13.16), indicating a district-wide tagging problem that emerged and may be moderating but warrants investigation into whether cleanup efforts are keeping pace.
evidence: Peak of 16 graffiti complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 1.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1,064% spike)
z-score of 13.16 is the highest statistical anomaly in entire dataset
Current status unclear—need to determine if complaints have subsided or if cleanup is masking ongoing problem
reporting_angles: Map the 16 graffiti complaints from 3 weeks ago to identify whether they cluster in specific neighborhoods or corridors
Interview Sanitation Department on response times and current graffiti removal workload in Belmont/East Tremont

themes_detail.label: Dead animal complaints
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints spiked to 10 LAST WEEK, a 900% increase from the 1.0 weekly baseline (z-score: 9.0), suggesting possible public health risk or sanitation service failure.
evidence: 10 dead animal complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (900% spike)
Converges with animal-in-park spike (1,100% increase 2 weeks ago), suggesting broader animal welfare or urban wildlife issue
reporting_angles: Contact Sanitation Department to identify locations and determine if removal is delayed
Investigate whether weather, disease, or environmental change is driving spike in dead animals

themes_detail.label: Root/sewer/sidewalk deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Root, sewer, and sidewalk condition complaints rose to 3 LAST WEEK, a 380% increase from the 0.6 weekly baseline (z-score: 3.41), potentially signaling infrastructure stress aligned with long-standing community board budget requests for DEP infrastructure upgrades.
evidence: 3 root/sewer/sidewalk complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (380% spike)
Aligns with Community Board's repeated budget request for 'Other capital budget request for DEP' (year-over-year ask)
Converges with flooring/stairs spike (29 complaints last week, 57% increase), suggesting building-level structural impact
reporting_angles: Interview DEP on backlog of sewer/root investigations in Belmont and East Tremont
Investigate whether recent weather or water events have accelerated root/sidewalk damage
